successors.name: Kingdom of Zimbabwe
successors.text: 'located at the confluence of the Shashe and Limpopo rivers in present day South Africa'; 'the state likely covered 30,000 km2' (a 98 km disc around Mapungubwe has the same area)

ledger.x: c. 1220: the Mapungubwe elite make Mapungubwe Hill their capital at the Shashe-Limpopo confluence. 'Around 1220, amid a dry period, the Mapungubwe elite moved to settle the top of Mapungubwe Hill'; the infobox says 'Established: c. 1220'.
c. 1220: the royal capital moves from K2 (Bambandyanalo) to Mapungubwe Hill: 'royal elites moved the capital to Mapungubwe (an old rainmaking site) and settled its flat-topped summit around 1220'.

c. 1300: the Limpopo-Shashe basin is abandoned and its land returns to nobody. 'Following unknown events and shifting trade routes north around 1300, Mapungubwe's population migrated elsewhere'; 'The basin was abandoned as people scattered northwest and south.'
c. 1300: Mapungubwe is abandoned and Great Zimbabwe, 'on the fringe of the Mapungubwe state', 'rose to become its successor'. Infobox: 'Mapungubwe Hill abandoned: c. 1300'.

certainty.note: No frontier is described; the 30,000 km2 area is the page's estimate and the outline is a disc.
